best_echo_sets.commentary: Offers a 10% unconditional Havoc DMG% boost alongside adding a large Havoc Damage hit to the Outro of the wearer. Also grants the incoming resonator a Havoc DMG% boost when the wearer uses their Outro. The set is better than Moonlit Clouds if and only if the equipped character's Echoes have endgame investment (with 9 or 10 CRIT substats total) and the character has a 5-star weapon equipped. If both conditions aren't met, Moonlit Clouds is a better choice.

main_echo_options.echo_commentary: Offers an unconditional 12% Havoc DMG and 12% Heavy Attack DMG boost when placed in the Main Echo slot, making it a solid choice for Havoc focused resonators who emphasize Heavy Attack damage and are looking to use the 5P Midnight Veil set bonus.

best_echo_sets.commentary: Offers a 10% unconditional Energy Regen% boost taking some pressure off your gear when aiming at ER breakpoints. Also upon using Outro, grants the next character switching in a 22.5% ATK boost, amplifying any of your main damage dealers burst windows.

main_echo_options.echo_commentary: Supportive Echo that can be run at the cost of a sizeable chunk of damage for the character who equips, trading personal gain for team benefits. Should always be used and immediately switch cancelled right before performing an Outro, leading to another DPS. When done so will grant the next character switching in 12% increased DMG% which when combined with the 5P Moonlit set which also grants 22.5% ATK% under the same conditions makes for a sizeable boost. While the echo does lower the damage of whoever wears it, it grants a massive chunk of energy on use usually saving 1 or sometimes even 2 Energy Regen sub stats that may otherwise be needed by the wearer allowing for some damage to be recovered.

best_weapons.commentary_details: Roccia's Signature gives her the best personal damage increases she can get thanks to a 48% Heavy DMG and 24.3% CRIT Rate bonus, making it her best in slot weapon.

best_weapons.commentary_details: Best no-gacha option for Roccia, simple ATK stat-stick with no passive to take advantage of whatsoever since it's Negative Status-related and Roccia plays in no such teams. This can be a temporary weapon choice, but to move away from this weapon and equip her with at least Pulsation Bracer as soon as possible, if you can.

cons: Outclassed in every team she's a part of (by Lynae, Qiuyuan or Lucilla), and easily replaced by 4-stars in every team she's a part of (either by Danjin or Sanhua), particularly without her Signature weapon, where she's just worse than 4-stars outright.
Low headroom for Swap Cancels due to a short rotation that relies on 3 mid-air moves that need to be chained one after the other following a specific attack (similar to Qiuyuan).
Signature is theoretically skippable, but she's so close in value to 4-star characters that she needs it to stand out from them.

Very inconsistent rotations before S1; again, a similar problem to Qiuyuan where if one of her mid-airs gets interrupted, her rotation slows down massively and this only stops happening at S1 or higher.
pros: Has a grouping utility that counts as an extra Echo Skill cast.
Has one of the best JP VAs and the cutest pet known to mankind.

sections.heading: Summary
paragraphs: Roccia is a 5-star Havoc Gauntlets buffer who specializes in buffing Basic/Havoc DMG-dealing characters, with a focus on AoE grouping and the nice feature of having 1 extra Echo Skill cast compared to regular characters. Her rotation is quite fast and features a lot of mid-air action with some decent personal damage and buffing, similar to other characters of the 1.x-early 2.x era.

sections.heading: Key Mechanics & Rotation
paragraphs: Roccia rotates on the principle of getting her Outro off as quickly as possible, like most supports and buffer-type characters. It provides 20% Havoc and 25% Basic DMG Amplification to the next character for 14s or until they are switched out, like most Hybrid Outros. To charge it up quickly, she needs to access some mid-air bouncing Heavy Attacks called "Real Fantasy", as all stages give a ton of Concerto upon landing, increasing as the chain goes on.

To cast them, she needs to use (and hence build up) Imagination, her Forte gauge split in 3 bars. Roccia can achieve this either by charging a Heavy Attack on the ground, which is rather slow (but at least not slower than most of her Basics), or rotate with an Intro (which chains into a Basic 4) and a Skill, each restoring one of the thirds, which is much faster. Her Skill and ground Heavy Attack are in fact the only ways Roccia has of casting her Real Fantasy bounces, so in case she gets interrupted, her Heavy Attack is your best bet. This will however, slow Roccia's rotation down significantly and is often grounds for resetting an endgame content run.

Her Ultimate also buffs the whole party's ATK by up to 200 for 30s based on her CRIT Rate (maxxing out at 70%) upon casting. And upon casting Outro, Roccia unlocks a special Utility called Magic Box (like the Grapple, Flight or Motorbike utilities, for example), which counts as an extra Echo Skill cast. It deals a flat 100 damage but can group small enemies with your incoming character while Roccia is off-field.

sections.heading: Meta Position & Conclusion
paragraphs: As you can see, we're already done explaining all of Roccia's buffs and essential rotation moves; she's an extremely simple character. But that's unfortunately not to her benefit. In the short rotation, Basic DMG buffing department, Sanhua is an extremely obvious pick that at S6 is already rivaling Roccia for her one use in Basic DMG buffing: Camellya. She already had a fully constituted team with Sanhua, and unfortunately for Roccia - who takes longer to rotate than the fastest Hybrid character in the entire game - her higher personal damage does not justify the rotation time increase, not to mention her buffs are barely better than Sanhua's for Camellya specifically (and in terms of Basic DMG buffing, that's all Roccia's good at). To make matters worse, her grouping is not necessary since Camellya already has some of the widest AoE attacks in the entire game with her spin, Ultimate and Forte Skill. Overall, regarding her Outro and grouping, Roccia only exists as a sidegrade to a completely free character. Not looking good there.

So let's shift the focus over to her personal damage and extra Echo Skill cast. She's a perfect fit for the Phrolova team: an ideal recipient for Phrolova's Outro, a party-wide ATK buff with her Ultimate, an extra Echo Skill cast to trigger an enhanced Hecate attack. Sure, her grouping is again not needed, since Hecate is the best crowd control utility in the entire game to date, but surely this makes Roccia good, right? Again, a missed opportunity. She's barely better than Danjin, not better than Shorekeeper, and definitely way worse than Qiuyuan and Lucilla.

And this unfortunately already exhausted Roccia's 2 "best" meta niches, if you can even call them that. Even with her Signature weapon equipped, Roccia's personal damage increases barely make her better than her 4-star competition. In conclusion, Roccia, since her release, has always been destined to fail. She never stood out, even in 2 teams that were built with her in mind, due to a lack of significant buffs and not enough unique features compared to the free alternatives Sanhua and Danjin, and stronger premium alternatives like Lynae (for Camellya) and Qiuyuan/Lucilla (for Phrolova). Overall, unless you're willing to pull Sequences for Roccia (which in itself is not even an optimal choice since you rather get Sequences on the DPS characters she supports or universal 3rd slots instead), unfortunately she's either a sidegrade to free characters at best, or a bad premium alternative at worst, making her one of the least valuable limited 5-stars in Wuthering Waves. Here's to hoping for a Roccia kit buff, because she needs one.

synergies.commentary: Roccia amplifies Havoc DMG by 20% and Basic Attack DMG by 25% on Outro, making the synergy with Camellya, who does those two damage types the most by far, extremely natural. Camellya's best in slot buffer, no doubt (despite being very competitive with Sanhua).

Roccia is one of the best third slot teammate to the Phrolova-Cantarella trio as she is the best recipient of Phrolova's Outro Skill which amplifies Havoc DMG and Heavy Attack DMG by 20% and 25% respectively, lining up with Roccia's damage types and allowing a trio with Cantarella to always upkeep high damage, making for a strong Phrolova team.

Roccia's 20% Havoc and 25% Basic Attack DMG Amplify on Outro are some of the best buffs Havoc Rover can receive, but additionally Roccia's grouping are very much appreciated with Havoc Rover's small AoE attacks that do big damage. Easily Havoc Rover's best buffer.

One of the usual Healing Support options that can slot into any team. Super easy to use, provides amazing team-wide ATK% buffs and 15% DMG Amplify with one of the fastest rotations in the game. Enjoy.

Similar to Verina, a premium Healing Support option who can not only slot into any team, but also provide insane 12.5% Crit Rate, 25% Crit DMG, 25% ATK and 15% DMG Amplify buffs to your whole team. One of the best but also easy to use characters in the game.
